problem: Given that ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ are the solutions to the equation $\operatorname{sec}⁡x=2$ for $-{360}^{∘}\le x<{0}^{∘},$ what is the numerical value of ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}?$
worked_solution:
Recall that $\operatorname{sec}⁡x=\frac{1}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}.$ Therefore, the given equation is equivalent to

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡x=\frac{1}{2}.
$$

First, we find the principal value:

$$
x=\operatorname{arccos}⁡(\frac{1}{2})={60}^{∘}
$$

Note that $x={60}^{∘}$ is not in the domain $-{360}^{∘}\le x<{0}^{∘}.$ To get a solution within the required domain, we subtract ${360}^{∘}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & ={60}^{∘}-{360}^{∘}=-{300}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Our first solution lies in the first quadrant and has a reference angle of ${\theta }_{R}={60}^{∘}.$ Since $\operatorname{cos}⁡x>0,$ the second solution must lie in the fouth quadrant, and it also has a reference angle ${\theta }_{R}={60}^{∘}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13977622/assets/9c8adbb0a1594ae5bacfab7f1f92993c67659839599e10ab46d5cf98896e3ec7.png)

A second solution $X$ lies in the $4$th quadrant, and we can find it using the reference angle as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}X & ={360}^{∘}-{\theta }_{R} \\  & ={360}^{∘}-{60}^{∘} \\  & ={300}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

Note that $X={300}^{∘}$ is not in the domain $-{360}^{∘}\le x<{0}^{∘}.$ To get a solution within the required domain, we subtract ${360}^{∘}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{3} & ={300}^{∘}-{360}^{∘}=-{60}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the solutions are $x=-{60}^{∘},-{300}^{∘}.$

Finally,

$$
{x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}=-60\cdot (-300)=18\,000
$$
